newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajik peace talks delayed until opposition arrive.
newsitem.headline: Tajik peace talks delayed until opposition arrive.

text.p: Peace talks in Moscow between the Tajik president and the leader of the former Soviet republic's Islamic opposition have been postponed until opposition leaders arrive in the Russian capital, officials said on Thursday.
The discussions had initially been expected to start at 9 a.m. (0600 GMT), to be followed by a news conference.

Russia's Interfax news agency quoted a Tajik government official as saying the talks had been postponed because exiled opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri had not yet arrived to meet Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov.

"Rakhmonov hopes this meeting will take place and will provide a breakthrough on the road to a final political settlement of the inter-Tajik conflict," Interfax quoted Rakhmonov's press secretary as saying.
Itar-Tass news agency, in a report from the Iranian capital Tehran, said Nuri had left there for Moscow on Thursday morning.

The two men, together with Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, had been due to discuss the most recent ceasefire agreement in the war-torn republic. Previous deals have been routinely flouted, sometimes immediately after they were signed.

The latest pact was agreed in talks in Afghanistan, but local officials have already reported fighting between government troops and the opposition in the Garm region, some 150 km (100 miles) east of the capital, Dushanbe.

In another incident casting doubts on the viability of the latest pact, United Nations military observers monitoring the implementation of the truce were subjected to a mock execution by Tajik government troops, the U.N. mission said on Wednesday.
"UNMOT military observers were subjected to blatant physical and verbal abuse (and) ordered to line up for execution," the observer mission said in a statement issued in Dushanbe.

Richard Morczynski, political officer with the U.N. observers, said in Dushanbe he still expected the meeting to take place. "Mr Nuri is expected to come to Moscow. If he arrives early this afternoon, the talks will take place today. If Mr Nuri arrives tomorrow, they will start then."
Opposition sources in Dushanbe said Nuri was delayed in the Iranian capital Tehran for political consultations with other Tajik opposition leaders.
Russian media said Moscow was opposed to Nuri's consultations in Iran and had wanted Nuri to fly direct from Afghanistan to Moscow.
